title: Ship evalctl v0.1 artifact harness
description:
evalctl v0.1 needs to prove a local-first agent evaluation path end to end: a code-review suite runs synchronously, an agent-under-test is invoked as a local runner, deterministic scorers grade the resulting workspace and response artifacts, and a self-contained run directory can regenerate the report without the original suite or runner environment.

The first release is intentionally narrow. It must not build hosted services, an inference proxy, async queueing, execution replay, mutating suite/case/scorer add commands, command scorers, or model-route provenance. The differentiated product is the workspace-scoring artifact, not prompt regression.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl init`, `validate`, `run`, `status`, `report`, `capabilities`, `schema`, and `robot-docs guide` support the synchronous code-review path.
- Every implemented JSON output uses the universal envelope and published exit-code/error-code contract.
- Runs produce portable run directories with suite snapshots, per-case inputs, runner artifacts, workspace manifests, derived scores, and reports.
- Deterministic built-in scorers include `workspace-diff` and can recompute reports from copied run artifacts.
- The v0.1 artifact replay success test passes from a copied run directory without invoking the original runner.

title: Implement CLI contract skeleton
description: The CLI needs a machine-first contract before behavior is implemented so agents can discover verbs, flags, schemas, exit codes, and follow-up commands without scraping human help text.
design:
Implement `capabilities --json`, `schema <verb> --json`, core `--help`, the universal JSON envelope, the code registry, the exit-code dictionary, and the `integrations` discoverability block for planned `spoolctl` and `inferctl` support.

Every `--json` result, including `capabilities` and `schema`, should be wrapped as `{ok, tool_version, data, meta, warnings, commands, errors}`. `meta.data_hash` is computed from canonicalized `data` with volatile fields excluded. Human rendering is a projection chosen only when stdout is a TTY and no explicit machine format was requested.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl capabilities --json` returns the universal envelope with `contract_version`, implemented verbs, flags, env vars, schemas, exit-code dictionary, code registry references, and integrations where `spoolctl` and `inferctl` are `available:false` and `planned:true`.
- `evalctl schema <verb> --json` returns the envelope for each implemented verb.
- All implemented verbs accept `--json`; `report --format json` is accepted as an alias for `report --json`.
- JSON stdout is parseable and contains no ANSI escapes; diagnostics and mirrored errors go to stderr.
- Golden tests pin `capabilities --json` and implemented verb schemas with volatile metadata excluded.

title: Implement artifact replay success test
description: The v0.1 ship gate is artifact replay: a second agent must be able to copy a run directory, regenerate the report, and recompute deterministic scorers without the original suite path or runner environment.
design: Build an acceptance harness that runs the code-review suite, copies the resulting run directory to a clean location without an `evals/` root and without invoking the runner, runs `evalctl report --run-dir <copied> --format json`, recomputes scorers from persisted artifacts, and compares the regenerated `data.report_hash` against the original.
acceptance_criteria:
- The harness exercises at least one passing and one failing case.
- Recomputed scorers use `suite-snapshot/`, `input.json`, `output.*`, `runner.json`, `workspace-before.json`, and `workspace-after.json`; original `score.json` is not trusted.
- The regenerated normalized report hash equals the original when artifacts are unchanged.
- No runner command is invoked during artifact replay.
- A changed artifact causes a report-hash mismatch or explicit validation error.

Treat `diff` as review material exposed through `EVALCTL_DIFF_FILE`; do not apply it to the workspace in v0.1.

title: Implement runner execution contract
description: The runner is the agent-under-test invocation, and v0.1 must execute it honestly as arbitrary local code while bounding reproducibility and artifact leakage.
design:
Support `runner.argv` with `shell:false` as the default and `runner.command` with `shell:true` as an explicit escape hatch. Exactly one form is valid for the selected mode. Default `cwd` to the per-case workspace. Inherit only `env_allowlist` variables and always inject `EVALCTL_CASE_FILE`, `EVALCTL_WORKSPACE`, `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE`, `EVALCTL_TASK_FILE`, and `EVALCTL_DIFF_FILE` when present.

Close stdin by default, with `runner.stdin:"task"` to pipe task text. Apply `timeout_seconds`, kill the process group on timeout, capture stdout/stderr/output up to `max_output_bytes`, and apply `redact_env_values` and `redact_patterns` before writing artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- `shell:false` executes argv without implicit shell joining; `$EVALCTL_*` substitution is performed only by evalctl.
- `shell:true` executes the explicit command through `sh -c` and is documented as the less-safe escape hatch.
- Runner spawn failures and timeouts mark the case `error`; ordinary nonzero process exits are captured and scored rather than treated as tool errors.
- Every `run` emits `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER` in the JSON envelope and prints the warning to stderr when appropriate unless the suite explicitly acknowledges it.
- Captured stdout, stderr, and output are truncated and redacted before persistence, with booleans recording whether truncation or redaction occurred.
close_reason: Implemented runner argv/shell validation, env injection, timeout/capture/redaction handling, and unsandboxed-runner warning support — commit 449ded0

title: Capture workspace manifests
description: The core differentiator is scoring the resulting workspace, so evalctl must capture structured before/after filesystem evidence rather than relying on textual diffs.
design: Walk the per-case workspace before and after runner execution to produce `workspace-before.json` and `workspace-after.json`. Derive `workspace-diff.json` from those manifests. Include untracked and ignored files. Represent files, directories, symlinks, and other special file types. Use POSIX-style relative UTF-8 paths with no `.` or `..` segments and no absolute paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Full manifests contain entries with `path`, `kind`, and file hashes where applicable.
- Directories are represented by presence; binary files are represented by sha256; symlinks are not followed and store target information.
- Unreadable or unsupported non-UTF-8 paths emit `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` and do not silently corrupt the manifest.
- `workspace-diff.json` identifies added, modified, and deleted paths from the two structured manifests.
- Textual `workspace.diff` is best-effort and never parsed by scorers.
close_reason: Implemented before/after workspace manifests, structured diff manifests, path normalization, symlink/special-file handling, and text diff projection — commit 449ded0

title: Implement deterministic built-in scorers
description: v0.1 must grade runs with deterministic local scorers that are credible without an LLM judge and can be recomputed from persisted artifacts.
design: Implement built-in scorers for `exact`, `contains`, `regex`, `json-schema`, `numeric-threshold`, `file-exists`, `exit-code`, and `workspace-diff`. Each scorer emits `{ok, score, label, findings}` and respects whether it is required or advisory. Built-in scorers consume persisted, redacted outputs and structured workspace manifests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each scorer has unit tests for pass, fail, and malformed-input behavior.
- `workspace-diff` matches `expect.files_changed` and `expect.files_forbidden` using glob semantics against `changed_paths[].path`.
- `exit-code` compares expected exit code against `runner.json` and does not conflate failed expectations with tool errors.
- Required scorer failures produce case status `fail`; scorer crashes or invalid scorer inputs produce case status `error`.
- Score output is stable and can be serialized into each case `score.json`.

title: Implement synchronous run orchestration
description: v0.1 needs one complete synchronous execution path that can run a suite, invoke runners, score cases, and continue through partial failures without depending on async infrastructure.
design:
Implement `evalctl run <suite> [--jobs N] [--timeout S] [--run-id <id>] [--fail-on-fail] [--json]`. Create a reservation for the run id, materialize a fresh workspace per case, execute cases with bounded concurrency, write artifacts, derive scores, update `manifest.json` atomically, and continue after case-level errors with `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.

Default `--jobs` to `min(CPU_count, 4)`. Sort iteration before serialization so JSON is deterministic regardless of completion order. Use `<UTC-timestamp>-<suite-name>` for default run ids. Reusing a completed matching run id returns the existing run; live reservations return `E_RUN_BUSY`; semantic clashes return `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run` produces a complete run directory under `evals/runs/` with a suite snapshot and per-case artifacts.
- Case errors do not abort the whole run; the run remains reportable and emits `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.
- Eval failures exit 0 by default and set `data.run.ok:false`; `--fail-on-fail` exits 6 when any case is not `pass`.
- A live reservation returns exit 4 with `E_RUN_BUSY` and a retry recommendation; a completed mismatched run id returns exit 5 with `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
- JSON output includes paste-ready follow-up commands only for implemented verbs.
close_reason: Implemented synchronous run orchestration with per-case workspaces, run directories, scoring, partial-run warnings, run-id reuse, and fail-on-fail exit behavior — commit 449ded0

title: Implement status and report commands
description: Agents need diagnose and triage commands that summarize run state, rank failures deterministically, and point to the exact artifacts needed for inspection.
design:
Implement `status <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--json]` and `report <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--format markdown|json] [--json]`. Resolve run ids under `evals/runs/`; accept copied standalone run directories through `--run-dir`. Rank report failures as `error` before `fail`, then by ascending aggregate numeric score, then case id.

`status` should include per-case state and a `recommended_action`. `report` should include aggregate scores, ranked failures, relative artifact links, and `data.report_hash` over the normalized report projection.
acceptance_criteria:
- `status` works for both local run ids and copied run directories.
- `report --format json` and `report --json` both return the universal envelope.
- Markdown reports are deterministic apart from explicitly volatile metadata.
- Ranked failures are ordered by error/fail class, aggregate score, and case id.
- `commands[]` contains only implemented follow-up commands such as regenerating a JSON report.

title: Fix spoolctl capability probe
description: Evalctl advertises optional queued execution through spoolctl, but the probe path currently assumes a simplified capabilities shape that differs from real spoolctl output. Real spoolctl reports its version at the JSON envelope top level and describes CLI flags as structured objects. Evalctl currently unwraps only the data payload and attempts to build a set directly from those flag objects, causing an internal TypeError before queued execution can start. This undermines the optional queue integration even though standalone evalctl execution remains useful.
design:
Keep the fix local to evalctl's spoolctl probing and test fixtures. Preserve the existing queue runner semantics for add, work, wait, show, and outcome mapping. Do not change spoolctl's capabilities contract or raise evalctl's minimum supported spoolctl version above 0.4.1.

The implementation should make real spoolctl envelope metadata available to the probe, normalize supported add flags from either string entries or structured objects, and distinguish soft capability discovery failures from hard queued-run failures.
acceptance_criteria:
- Evalctl capabilities reports real compatible spoolctl as available when spoolctl is on PATH.
- Evalctl queued runs can pass the probe and execute through compatible real or real-shaped spoolctl.
- Incompatible or malformed spoolctl probe responses never surface as Python tracebacks, TypeError, or generic internal errors.
- Capabilities discovery failures remain soft degradation: evalctl capabilities exits successfully with spoolctl unavailable.
- Queued run and queued resume probe failures remain hard evalctl envelope errors.
- No changes are required in spoolctl.
notes: CLOSED: Spoolctl probe compatibility epic complete. d2efea7 added envelope-preserving spoolctl JSON helper, normalized probe parsing for real/compact capability shapes, updated fake spoolctl fixture, added focused probe regressions, updated queued regression, and validated with full unittest suite plus real-source spoolctl smoke.

title: Add spoolctl JSON runner helper
description: Evalctl currently has one helper that both runs spoolctl and unwraps the returned JSON envelope. The capabilities probe needs access to envelope-level metadata such as tool_version, while the existing queued execution paths should continue receiving unwrapped data and preserving their current exit-code behavior.
design:
In evalctl/cli.py, add a low-level helper such as run_spoolctl_json(args, allow_exit_codes=None) that returns (returncode, payload). This helper should invoke the spoolctl binary, default allow_exit_codes to {0}, keep the wait path able to pass {0, 6}, map exit code 4 to E_JOB_TRANSIENT, map other disallowed exit codes to E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE, parse stdout as JSON, and map json.JSONDecodeError to E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE.

Preserve the current ordering: validate the process exit code before parsing JSON. A nonzero spoolctl process with a structured JSON error envelope should still surface through evalctl as the existing generic command-failed incompatibility message rather than exposing spoolctl's internal error code.

Update spoolctl_json() to call the new helper while preserving its current behavior: unwrap ok:true envelopes, allow the existing returncode==6 exception for wait results, reject ok:false envelopes when returncode is not 6, return raw object payloads if already non-envelope objects, and reject non-object parsed JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing spoolctl_json() call sites keep their behavior for add, work, wait, show, and wait's exit-6 outcome path.
- Invalid JSON from spoolctl maps to E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE.
- Exit code 4 from spoolctl maps to E_JOB_TRANSIENT.
- Disallowed nonzero exit codes map to E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE before JSON parsing.
- The new helper exposes both return code and full payload so probe_spoolctl can inspect envelope-level fields.
notes: CLOSED: Added run_spoolctl_json() and preserved spoolctl_json() compatibility behavior. Full unittest suite and real-source spoolctl smoke passed before close.
close_reason: Added envelope-preserving spoolctl JSON runner helper while preserving existing queue semantics — commit d2efea7

title: Normalize spoolctl probe parsing
description: The spoolctl capabilities probe currently reads version fields only from unwrapped data and assumes add flags are plain strings. Real spoolctl uses top-level envelope tool_version and structured flag objects, so evalctl must normalize the real shape while retaining compatibility with the older compact string-flag shape.
design:
Update probe_spoolctl() to call the envelope-preserving helper from the previous task. Use the existing envelope discriminator: isinstance(payload, dict) and "ok" in payload. For envelope payloads, require ok:true and object data. Decide explicitly whether non-envelope raw object capabilities output should remain supported; if it remains supported, add a test for that path, otherwise reject it as E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE.

Extract the version from envelope-level tool_version first, then data-level tool_version, then data-level version. Treat envelope-level tool_version as authoritative when present, including when reporting integration version through capabilities_data(). Extract contract_version from capabilities data.

Add a small normalizer such as spoolctl_flag_names(flags) that accepts a list of strings or a list of objects with string "flag" fields and returns a set of flag names. Unknown entries should be ignored, so malformed flags degrade to missing required flags rather than crashing. Keep the required probe criteria: version >= 0.4.1, contract_version == "1", and add flags include --cwd, --env, and --max-crashes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real-shaped capabilities with top-level tool_version and structured add flags are accepted.
- Compact capabilities with data-level version and string add flags remain accepted.
- Envelope-level tool_version wins over conflicting data-level version fields.
- Missing required add flags return E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE instead of raising TypeError.
- Missing or malformed version fields reject cleanly without an internal error.
- The returned probe data includes a normalized version value usable by capabilities_data().
notes: CLOSED: probe_spoolctl now reads full capabilities envelopes, treats envelope tool_version as authoritative, supports compact/raw compatibility shapes, and normalizes add flags from strings or structured objects. Verified by focused probe tests, full unittest suite, and real-source spoolctl smoke.
close_reason: Normalized spoolctl capability probe parsing for real envelopes, compact responses, and structured flags — commit d2efea7

title: Capture inferctl preflight provenance
description: evalctl v0.4 should optionally record inferctl control-plane readiness and selected-route context before each runner execution, without changing runner behavior or report scoring. Provenance capture must be best-effort: absence, incompatibility, preflight policy blocks, and capture failures should produce warnings and artifacts where possible, while standalone evaluation still completes.
design:
Add `run --inferctl-task TASK` for fresh runs. Validate the task token before invoking a subprocess. Probe inferctl once per run using short-timeout `inferctl capabilities --json`; support both raw data and envelope shapes. Compatible v0.4 provenance requires `preflight`; `route` is optional. Capabilities absence or incompatibility produces one run warning and actual mode `none`.

Capture mode is hardcoded to `["preflight"]`. Invoke `inferctl preflight <task> --prompt-file <case task file> --allow-fallback --json` after case workspace preparation and before synchronous runner execution or queued spoolctl enqueue. Do not call `inferctl route` in v0.4. Bound capture concurrency independently from runner `--jobs`. The capture helper must never raise; convert subprocess errors, timeouts, JSON parse failures, OS errors, and unexpected exceptions into `W_INFERCTL_CAPTURE_FAILED`.

Store complete observed JSON outputs atomically in per-case artifacts. Write case-level `inferctl-preflight.json`, `inferctl-provenance.json`, and optional `inferctl-error.json`. Add run-level and case-level `provenance.inferctl` blocks to manifests. Extract best-effort summaries such as selected backend, selected model, ready, runnable, warning codes, and error codes. Emit `W_INFERCTL_PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED` when parseable preflight data says the case is non-runnable or policy/readiness blocked; ordinary fallback selected under `--allow-fallback` is recorded but not a warning.

Keep `report_hash` unchanged by leaving report projection unchanged. Rehydrate completed-case provenance during resume from sidecar artifacts, attach provenance to synthesized runner-error manifest entries when present, and keep replay capture disabled unless replay threading and tests are explicitly implemented.

- With compatible fake inferctl, `run --inferctl-task code` writes preflight and provenance artifacts for every executed case.

- `report_hash` matches an equivalent run without inferctl when runner and scorer outputs are identical.
- With inferctl absent, run succeeds, emits one `W_INFERCTL_ABSENT`, writes no inferctl artifacts, and records actual mode `none`.
- With capabilities missing `preflight`, run succeeds with one `W_INFERCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`.
- Non-runnable or policy-blocked preflight data on nonzero exit still lets the runner execute and records `W_INFERCTL_PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED`.
- Fallback route selection under `--allow-fallback` is recorded without emitting `W_INFERCTL_PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED`.
- Preflight exits with parseable JSON store artifacts and classify warnings from payload content.
- Preflight garbage output or timeout still lets execution and scoring proceed and emits exactly one capture-failed warning in synchronous and queued modes.
- Capture concurrency is bounded independently from runner jobs.
- Queued spoolctl runs capture inferctl artifacts before enqueue and preserve score/report parity.
- Runner failure after successful capture produces a synthesized error manifest entry with case-level inferctl provenance.
- Resume preserves terminal-case provenance and captures only pending cases.
- Replay without explicit provenance support produces no `inferctl-*` files and no orphan provenance artifacts.

description: Run-scoped values such as creation time, execution parameters, suite identity, and queue provenance are currently only held in memory until the final manifest is written. A crash before finalization loses the information needed to reconstruct the manifest consistently.
design: Split run execution into plan, execute, and finalize stages. Write a `run.json` sidecar exactly once at run start before any case executes. Store schema version, run id, created timestamp, full suite identity as sorted `(case_id, input_hash)` pairs, execution settings, replay provenance, and optional queue provenance. Finalization should project from `run.json` plus case artifacts rather than call-time locals. Update `now_iso` so `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` controls timestamps when set. Preserve existing cleanup for failures before durable resume state exists, but leave a run resumable when `run.json` and at least one terminal marker exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh runs write `run.json` before case execution and never overwrite it for an existing incomplete run.
- `run.json` stores the full suite identity list, not only a case count.
- Manifest finalization derives run-scoped fields from `run.json`.
- `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` produces stable `created_ts` values used by both `run.json` and `manifest.json`.
- Plain synchronous `report_hash` is unchanged from the existing sample-suite expectation.
- Durability sidecars do not appear in `report_data` and do not affect report hashes.
- A prepare-phase failure before resumable state removes the run dir; a failure after durable state plus at least one terminal marker leaves a resumable dir.

title: Add reservation TTL heartbeat
description: An incomplete run directory currently behaves like a permanent reservation. After a process crash, later invocations cannot distinguish a live run from abandoned state.
design: Add a liveness-only `.reservation.json` sidecar containing run id, process diagnostics, start timestamp, heartbeat timestamp, and TTL seconds. Start a background heartbeat during run and resume execution. Use TTL-based liveness for contention: live reservations return `E_RUN_BUSY`; stale reservations are reclaimable only through `run --resume`; plain `run` against stale incomplete state returns `E_RUN_BUSY` with a resume hint. Clear the reservation after successful finalization.
acceptance_criteria:
- `--reservation-ttl` is accepted on `run` and defaults to 3600 seconds.
- A concurrent invocation against a live run returns `E_RUN_BUSY` with exit 4.
- A long-running case stays live because the heartbeat updates independently of case boundaries.
- After TTL expiry, `run --resume <run-id>` reclaims stale state and emits `W_RESERVATION_RECLAIMED`.
- Plain `run --run-id <id>` against a stale incomplete dir returns `E_RUN_BUSY` and does not clobber the run.
- Successful finalization clears the reservation sidecar.

title: Implement run resume
description: Interrupted runs cannot be completed without discarding work. Users need `run --resume <run-id>` to reuse the original run metadata and suite snapshot, skip terminal cases, execute only pending cases, and finalize the same run id.
design: Add `--resume <run-id>` as a flag on `run`. For completed runs, return the existing summary plus `W_RESUME_NOTHING_PENDING` without rewriting the manifest. For incomplete runs, require `suite-snapshot/`, valid `run.json`, and a stale or absent reservation. Verify `run.json.suite_identity` matches the suite snapshot. Use persisted execution parameters rather than resume-invocation `--jobs` or `--timeout`. Finalize zero-pending incomplete runs without re-executing cases. Add `E_RUN_CORRUPT` for malformed run metadata.

title: Add command-scorer protocol
description:
`run_scorer` is a closed dispatch over eight deterministic built-in scorers; there is no
way to score a case with an external program. v0.2 adds a `command` scorer type — the
external scorer seam that is also the future LLM-judge seam — so a suite can score a case
by running an arbitrary program that emits a JSON verdict. Because report and replay
recompute case status from artifacts and never trust `score.json`, a non-deterministic
external scorer must be captured as an artifact, not re-executed.
design:
Add a `command` branch to `run_scorer`, and thread `case_dir: Path` and `execute: bool`
through `score_case` and `run_scorer`. `run_case` calls with `execute=True`;
`recompute_case_score` calls with `execute=False`.

Scorer config entry:
`{"name":"command","id":"<unique>","required":bool,"argv":[...]|"command":"...","shell":bool,"timeout_seconds":N}`.
The `id` is required for command scorers (a suite may have several, all named
`"command"`), must be path-safe (no separators, no `..`, no unsafe filename chars), and
names the verdict artifact.

Execute path (run time): invoke once per case with `EVALCTL_CASE_FILE` (persisted
`input.json`), `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE` (persisted `output.txt`), and `EVALCTL_WORKSPACE`;
cwd is the case workspace; argv/command gets the same `$EVALCTL_*` substitution as the
runner. Persist the parsed verdict to `cases/<case_id>/scorers/<id>.json`. This artifact
is a runner-class input, captured once, never regenerated.

Replay path (report time): read the persisted verdict artifact; never execute. Deterministic
scorers keep recomputing as today.

Process hardening (mirror the runner): `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)`
with `os.killpg` process-group kill on timeout; `timeout_seconds` from a named default
when omitted; byte-capped stdout/stderr with decode-and-replace; apply the suite's
redaction patterns and redacted env values before persisting; write capped/redacted
`cases/<case_id>/scorers/<id>.stdout.txt` and `.stderr.txt` for debugging.

Verdict normalization: stdout must parse as exactly one JSON object after trimming
whitespace (extra non-whitespace output is a scorer error); `ok` required boolean;
`score` required finite numeric constrained to 0.0..1.0 (reject NaN/Infinity and
out-of-range); `label` required string, normalized to `"pass"`/`"fail"` from `ok` when
missing/empty; `findings` required list, string entries normalized to `{"why": <string>}`.
`error:true` from a zero-exit process is a case error.

Status mapping: required scorer `ok:false,error:false` -> case `fail`; advisory scorer
`ok:false` does not fail the case; `error:true` or any normalization failure -> case
`error` regardless of `required`. A nonzero exit, timeout, or unparseable/invalid verdict
produces a scorer result carrying `error:true` and `error_code:"E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED"`,
which drives the case to `status:"error"` via the existing `s.get("error")` path — never
an orchestrator abort.

Carry the scorer `id` through every scores projection: the result object, the manifest
case entry, and the report/status failure projections — omitting the key when absent so
deterministic-only suites' `report_hash` is byte-unchanged.

Add `E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED` to the code registry (class `tool-env`, surface `score_json`
as a machine-token parallel to `runner_json`, where `["run","replay"]`); keep the
existing envelope-abort `E_SCORER_FAILED` distinct. A command-scorer is arbitrary local
code covered by the existing always-in-envelope unsandboxed-runner warning.
acceptance_criteria:
- A suite with a passing command-scorer scores the case pass and writes `cases/<id>/scorers/<id>.json`.
- Copy the run dir, delete the scorer binary, and `report --run-dir <copy>` reproduces the original `report_hash` (verdict is an artifact, never re-executed).
- Two command scorers, one passing and one failing: the report identifies the failing scorer by `id`.
- Invalid `score` type, NaN/Infinity, missing `ok`, extra stdout, and `error:true` from a zero-exit process each yield case `error`; a required scorer `ok:false,error:false` yields `fail`; an advisory scorer `ok:false` does not fail the case.
- A nonzero-exit or non-JSON scorer yields `status:"error"`, `W_PARTIAL_RUN`, run exits 0 (6 under `--fail-on-fail`), no envelope `errors[]`.
- Command-scorer timeout kills the process group; stdout/stderr are byte-capped and redacted in the persisted debug artifacts.

title: Implement replay --failed execution replay
description:
Only artifact replay exists today: a copied run dir reproduces its report, but there is
no way to re-execute a failed case after fixing the runner or fixtures. `replay --failed`
re-runs only the failed/errored cases of a prior run against the current suite, into a
fresh run linked to the source, so a fix turns a red case green in a new run. `manifest.replayed_from`
is already reserved but never populated.
design:
Add `evalctl replay --failed <source-run-id|--run-dir PATH> [--suite S] [--run-id NEW] [--force] [--json]`
with its own source parser — do NOT reuse `resolve_run`, which strips only
`--run-dir`/`--format` and would misread `--failed`/`--run-id`. Exactly one source is
required (positional id XOR `--run-dir`; both or neither -> `E_CASE_INVALID`). `--run-id`
is destination-only. `--failed` is the only selector in v0.2; missing it -> `E_CASE_INVALID`.

Select failed targets from `report_data(source_run)` (the recomputed projection), NOT
from stored `manifest.cases[].status` — the manifest status is a run-time summary, while
the authoritative reportable state is recomputed from artifacts (command-scorer verdicts
included). Targets are cases whose recomputed `status != "pass"`. Use the manifest only
for provenance and id/artifact metadata.

Resolve the current suite: default to `manifest.suite.name` resolved the way `run`
resolves a suite; `--suite <suite-or-path>` overrides (needed because the manifest stores
only suite name+hash, `suite.json.name` can differ from the directory, and a copied
`--run-dir` may sit where `evals/suites/<name>` does not exist). Resolution failure ->
`E_SUITE_NOT_FOUND` with a hint to pass `--suite`. Intersect targets with the current
suite's cases; a selected case absent from the current suite is dropped with
`W_REPLAY_CASE_ABSENT`, never fabricated.

Produce a coherent PARTIAL run over exactly the re-executed cases: fresh run dir (default
run id `<source>-replay-<UTC-ts>`, `--run-id` overrides), snapshot the CURRENT suite,
re-run the selected cases through the shared executor. Factor the executor loop out of
`command_run` into a shared `execute_cases(...)` helper both call. Write the manifest with
`replayed_from = <source run_id>` and `cases[]` = the replayed subset; `manifest.suite.case_count`
is the subset count, explicitly not the full current suite count. Emit the always-in-envelope
unsandboxed-runner warning (replay re-executes runner code) and `W_PARTIAL_RUN` when any
replayed case errors.

Overwrite gating: fresh dir needs no gate. `--run-id` naming an existing completed run
requires `--force`; without it -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). `--force` does not remove a
busy reservation dir (stays `E_RUN_BUSY`). Reject destination == source even under
`--force` (e.g. `--run-id r1` on source `r1`, or a `--run-dir` destination resolving to

title: Add suite add authoring verb
description:
Suites can only be created by `init_project`, which scaffolds the fixed sample. There is
no way to create a new empty suite from the CLI, forcing hand-authored JSON. `suite add`
creates a minimal valid suite that `case add` and `scorer add` then fill.
design:
Add `evalctl suite add <name> [--runner-argv "..."] [--runner-command "..."] [--shell] [--json]`.
Create `evals/suites/<name>/` with a minimal valid `suite.json` (name,
`cases: "cases.jsonl"`, a runner block from the flags with the v0.1 defaults for
`timeout_seconds`, `max_output_bytes`, `env_allowlist`, empty redaction), an empty
`cases.jsonl`, and a `fixtures/` dir. Runner form is mutually exclusive (`--runner-argv`
XOR `--runner-command`+`--shell`), validated up front the way `validate_suite` validates
runner config.

The `<name>` is path-contained: reject path separators, `..`, empty segments, or any name
that normalizes outside `evals/suites` with `E_CASE_INVALID`.

Atomic multi-file creation: a new suite is a directory plus multiple files, so per-file
atomic writes do not prevent a half-created suite dir. If the destination already exists,
decide idempotent-match vs conflict before writing anything. Otherwise build a temporary
sibling dir under `evals/suites/`, populate it fully, run `validate_suite` on it, then
`os.replace`/rename into place only on success.

Idempotency: an existing suite dir with a byte-identical `suite.json` -> `created:false`,
return name. Existing with different content -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). Never overwrite
an authored suite. An empty suite (zero cases) validates as `case_count:0, valid:true`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `suite add demo --runner-argv "python3 $EVALCTL_WORKSPACE/r.py"` creates `evals/suites/demo/{suite.json,cases.jsonl,fixtures/}`, and `validate demo` passes with `case_count:0`.
- Re-running the identical command -> `created:false`.
- The same name with a different runner -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5.
- A name with a path separator or `..` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`.
- A forced failure mid-creation leaves no half-built suite dir (temp-dir-and-rename).
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added suite add with safe suite names, runner flag grammar, idempotent existing-suite detection, and temp-dir creation with validation-before-rename.
- Added CLI tests for creation, validation, idempotency, conflict, invalid names, runner grammar, and rollback via injected validation failure.

title: Add case add authoring verb
description:
Cases exist only as hand-written JSONL lines; no verb appends one. `case add` appends a
valid case to an existing suite, assigning and returning its id, so a suite can be built
entirely from the CLI.
design:
Add `evalctl case add <suite> --task "..." --workspace <path> [--id ID] [--diff <path>] [--expect-json '<json>'] [--json]`.
Append one line to `cases.jsonl` in the existing on-disk form (one `stable_json(case)`
per line, trailing newline) so unrelated cases do not churn.

Canonical construction order (this is how idempotency is judged): parse flags -> build the
body WITHOUT id -> compute the generated id if `--id` is absent (the same rule
`load_cases` uses: content-hash slice) -> set `id` -> serialize with `stable_json`. Retry
comparison is against that canonical body including the generated id, so a retry never
looks different merely because one object had an explicit id and the other did not.

`--expect-json` parses into the case's `expect` field, not a new `expect_json` field; an
absent/empty `--expect-json` omits `expect` entirely (does not write `"expect": {}`) and
retries must match that choice.

Path containment: reject absolute `--workspace`/`--diff` and any relative path containing
`..` with `E_CASE_INVALID`; store normalized POSIX-relative paths. The workspace (and diff
if given) must also exist under the suite dir, matching the validator.

Idempotency: an existing case whose canonical body matches -> `created:false`, return id.
Same id, different canonical body -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). Reuse the existing
duplicate-id guard. Run `validate_suite` after the write; on failure roll back the
appended line by restoring the prior file bytes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `case add demo --task "do X" --workspace fixtures/x` (fixture created beforehand) appends one valid line, returns the id, and `validate demo` reports `case_count` incremented.
- Running the same command again without `--id` -> `created:false` and `cases.jsonl` byte-identical (canonical-body comparison).
- Same id, changed task -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5.
- `--workspace ../x`, an absolute `--workspace`, or a nonexistent `--workspace` -> `E_CASE_INVALID` exit 1, no line written.
- Unrelated cases' lines are byte-unchanged (no hash churn).
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added case add with canonical generated ids, expect JSON parsing into expect, path containment, idempotency/conflict checks, append-only JSONL writes, validation, and rollback.
- Added CLI tests for valid append, no-id retry, conflict, rejected paths, no-write failures, and preserving unrelated case lines.

title: Add scorer add authoring verb
description:
Scorers can only be configured by hand-editing the `scorers` array in `suite.json`.
`scorer add` appends a scorer entry (built-in deterministic or a command scorer),
completing the CLI-only authoring loop.
design:
Add `evalctl scorer add <suite> --name <scorer> [--required|--advisory] [--id ID] [--command "..."|--argv "..."] [--shell] [--timeout N] [--json]`.
Append to `suite.json`'s `scorers[]`, atomically rewriting `suite.json` preserving the
existing `indent=2, sort_keys=True` form so unrelated keys do not churn.

Validate `--name` against the known deterministic set plus `command`; unknown ->
`E_CASE_INVALID`. For `--name command`, a unique path-safe `--id` and a runner form are
required (the id names the per-case verdict artifact consumed by the command-scorer path).

Uniqueness keys: a deterministic scorer is keyed by `name` (built-ins carry no id — a
second entry with the same name and different config is a conflict, not a legal
double-count that would skew the aggregate); a command scorer is keyed by `id`.
Byte-identical entry already present -> `created:false`. Matching key with different
config -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). A new command-scorer id colliding with an existing
one -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT`. An `--id` with path separators or unsafe filename chars ->
`E_CASE_INVALID`. Run `validate_suite` after the write; roll back on failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- `scorer add demo --name exact --required` appends the entry and `validate` still passes.
- `scorer add demo --name command --id judge1 --argv "..."` appends a command-scorer entry usable by the command-scorer path.
- Re-adding an identical entry -> `created:false`.
- `scorer add demo --name contains --required` then `scorer add demo --name contains --advisory` -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` exit 5, `suite.json` unchanged (built-in key is `name`).
- A conflicting command `--id`, an unknown scorer name, or an `--id` containing `/` behaves as specified (`E_RUN_CONFLICT` for id-config clash; `E_CASE_INVALID` for unknown name or unsafe id).
